Maintain WATCH for broader sector confirmation, but initiate small longs on these movers for tactical exposure.

Regulatory tightening on raw mineral exports is forcing upstream miners to invest in domestic smelting, creating durable cost advantages for early movers in the processing chain.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's revised RUPTL (2024-2034) mandates 60% renewable capacity additions, creating a durable pipeline for solar and geothermal developers amid coal phase-down pressures.
The upcoming carbon exchange and mandatory emissions trading for coal plants will monetize offsets, boosting project economics for climate-tech firms with verified credits.
Foreign capital inflows into ASEAN green infrastructure are accelerating, with Indonesia's nickel and geothermal resources positioning it as a critical supply chain hub for global decarbonization.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows a mild pullback, but the US utility uptick signals global capital rotation into defensive climate-tech. Focus on domestic catalysts: the new RUPTL grid plan and carbon trading launch. Accumulate on dips in solar and geothermal plays, as policy tailwinds and foreign investment mandates drive structural demand through 2025.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class consumption in Indonesia continues to drive premiumization in hygiene and personal care products, benefiting niche players like KLIN and SPRE.
Government push for downstreaming and local content in FMCG packaging is creating structural tailwinds for specialty chemical firms such as AGAR and TFCO.
Weak rupiah and elevated food inflation are pressuring mass-market FMCG margins, but companies with strong pricing power in essential categories (e.g., OILS, PSDN) can maintain resilience.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector underperformed today (-1.60%) vs US peers (+0.48%), but selective names like AGAR (+24.75%) and KLIN (+10%) surged on idiosyncratic catalysts. Maintain a WATCH stance: focus on bottom-up plays in hygiene and specialty foods, as broad macro headwinds from weak rupiah and slowing domestic demand persist.
